answer: A proof of work over challenge words only holds if the answer cannot be produced without real effort. Here the server hands out tide, basalt and raven, and a responder has to write fresh prose that uses them naturally. The cheap shortcut is reusing a stored answer or dropping the words into a fixed template, so the verifier should reject near duplicates of past submissions. An attacker then pays for a language model call each epoch plus the cost of rejected drafts, which turns every reward into a metered expense instead of free output.
